ELI5: Why Magic (MTG) cards are so damn expensive?

Like anything of value the primary factor in its cost is scarcity. The original run of MTG cards had a very small print, therefore very few are left in any sort of decent condition. This leads to higher prices for people looking to collect.

Building upon that is also the fact that you had Common-1 to Common-3, Uncommon-1 to Uncommon-3, Rare-1 and Rare-2, then of course Mythics. WotC claims that they did away with the c-1 to c-3 and u-1 to u-3, but it's obviously prevalent that you still have r-1 and r-2 rares.

http://mtg.wikia.com/wiki/Rarity_level

Everyone wants their cut (so coke from columbia get 600% margin when travel to some island from where it's smuggled to US, where it get another few xxx% margin, then to the dealers with another margin and then - shitty, mixed with lidocaine - to clients with another margin.

THIS WILL NOT BE AS THOUGH YOU'RE FIVE. It's incredibly difficult to explain some of the nuances as it deals with human behavior coupled with wants and economics therein. I've done my best but maybe someone can ELY5.

The competitive aspect of it. It's human nature to win. It's human nature to be better than. It's human nature to have the best. Those coupled with the playable cards either being rare or mythic rare or not printed anymore as they were released in magic's first few sets adds to the value. In addition few rares/mythic rares are actually good enough to be played - let alone hold the rarity.

When a metagame [the set of best decks at the current time makes up what's called the metagame] evolves and develops after a new set is release the cards in the new set may work amazing with much older cards which then make them see play in the older formats. The formats are in order of oldest to newest: vintage, legacy, modern, standard. Standard rotates at max two blocks. Blocks generally contain two sets. These two blocks cover a two year period. Modern covers since magic cards received "modern" updated borders and frames on the cards. Legacy allows all cards but has banned and restricted lists. Vintage allows all cards minus the few cards from the early days which make you do weird things - like Ante cards where a card you own is wagered - it also has a restricted list which is the legacy banned list but you can only have one of as opposed to the standard 4 of restriction.

Now realize back in the early days print runs were extremely small compared to now. Also with time the cards will begin to wear and sadly become unplayable or completely destroyed. It's in its 21st year I believe. 21 years later cards which there are only a few thousand of are pretty expensive because of all of the above.

I forgot to mention: as standard is only the most up to date two blocks and at most two years for the running time of when a block gets released. Standard has very little impact on cards beyond the two years they're relevant in standard. Whereas legacy and vintage rule them all. A card such as force of will which defines legacy and keeps it stable from turn 1 combo wins [yes, possible dozens of ways]. Won't ever see play in modern, nor in standard unless it's reprinted. Yet it carries a $100 price tag because the formats it's most heavily used in - vintage, legacy - allow for extremely rare cards, which it also is. So seeing as it's one of the best cards in magic, balances the format, and while rare isn't as rare as cards that go with it [underground sea, tarmogoyf] one can see how the prices just keep going up as if it's better than card X, and card X already has a value greater than the card at hand does then the card at hand will be very valuable.
